text: Full-suite run: all 63 rows of SeatMap_TestCases.csv (GulfAir / KSA, staging ndc-integration-stg-ne-3). Every row was executed or explicitly classified: 29 fresh Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (or Hold) chains were built for them (about 285 API calls in total, several chains run in parallel), the rest are read-only checks of shared seat maps, documentation rows or rows that cannot run for GulfAir (no bundle/ancillary capability, SeatAfterHold and FareConfirmAfterHold unsupported, no forcing mechanism, other suppliers out of scope). HEADLINE: BUG-16 (Book returns an error while silently creating the booking) did NOT reproduce - all 16 Book calls returned a clean 200 with a PNR (34-56 seconds each) and so did the 3 BookAfterHold calls. All other previously open defects reproduced unchanged, and one NEW defect was found (BUG-18: Retrieve under-reports the per-passenger seat total on multi-seat bookings). Environment note: GulfAir returns an empty seatMapDetails (0 rows) for departures from about 2027-08-03 and no offers after about mid-July 2027, so all chains use May-June 2027 dates. The disk log was written in batches after each group of calls rather than per test case in real time, so each test case's reporting_started_at/reporting_ended_at brackets a real JSONL append + Markdown re-render taken at write-up time, not at verdict time. BND-02, BND-03, BND-04, BIZ-02 and VAL-08 were re-recorded once after a wider scan of all seat maps found AvailableFree live. The x-api-key is never written to the log; raw OriginalSupplierRequest/Response payloads (credentials, recipient details) are replaced by a redaction marker.

summary: Retrieve under-reports the per-passenger seat total on a multi-seat booking: paxTotalSeatAmount counts only one seat, so paxTotalAmount and the sum of the passenger totals fall short of priceDetails.totalAmount. The Book response for the same booking is correct.
expected_value: paxTotalSeatAmount {"amount":120,"currency":"SAR"} for two 60.00 seats, paxTotalAmount 1730.00, matching the Book response
impact: A caller reading a booking back through Retrieve sees a seat total (60.00 instead of 120.00) and a per-passenger fare (1670.00 instead of 1730.00) that no longer add up to the booking total, so any invoice, refund or reconciliation built from the passenger lines is short by the missing seat(s). Not present in Round 6 (a round-trip Retrieve showed 240 for two 120 seats), so this looks like a regression.
evidence: Round-trip pnr OOERGR (seats 14C + 14D, 60.00 each): Book paxTotalSeatAmount 120 / paxTotalAmount 1730; Retrieve (called twice) paxTotalSeatAmount 60 / paxTotalAmount 1670 while passengerSeats lists both seats and priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is 120 / totalAmount 1730. Two-passenger round trip pnr OOBWZB (four seats): Book per-passenger seat total 100 each; Retrieve 60 each, per-passenger totals 1670 + 1670 = 3340 vs totalAmount 3420. One-seat booking ORUXWA is unaffected (60 = 60).

evidence: omit supplier 400 "Select a valid Supplier"; omit credentialsSelector 400; omit selectedOfferId 400 "The SelectedOfferId field is required."; omit ResponseId 200 with 30 rows.

summary: GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector).

impact: credentialsSelector is the per-tenant boundary; a caller holding an offerId/responseId from one tenant (KSA) can read that offer's seat map through another tenant's selector (UAE), so cross-tenant isolation rests only on offer IDs being unguessable. Other offer-consuming endpoints were not tested.
